title.narrative: Nam Ngum River Basin Development Sector Project (Additional Financing)

description.narrative: In response to the government's request, the Asian Development Bank approved the additional financing project to consolidate and expand the activities initiated under the current project, Nam Ngum River Basin Development Sector Project. The additional financing project will modify and scale-up the well-performing operations, particularly participatory sub-basin management to strengthen integrated water resources management (IWRM) capacity at the district level, consolidate khet (village cluster) extension service center and village development revolving fund operations, and expand promising agricultural support services to benefit additional villages in remote parts of the Nam Ngum River Basin (NNRB).

title.narrative: District development plans updated to incorporate sub-basin management concept.

description.narrative: Integrated watershed management improved in NNRB

title.narrative: Loan 2780: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 17 Jun 2022

Progress Toward Outcome: The project outcome has been partially achieved. The concept of IWRM was achieved by the original project (L1933). The concept continued to be integrated into the 8th NSEDP and DWR mandate at the time of additional financing. However, the remained key indicators are not yet achieved. These include (i) incorporation of the sub-basin management concept into the district development plans and (ii) income estimation in 50 additional villages increased only 20% which was lower than target (60%).
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Dec 2014: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents//33356-014-iee-14.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1: all indicators under this output are achieved (i.e. completion of 3 workshops with 37% female participated; 5 sub-basin management plans.
Output 2: all achieved. Completion of updating of 10 WLCPs and handing over to the district authorities.
Output 3: Mostly achieved. rice yield increased by 3.53t/ha. buffaloes increased by 15.6%. pigs increased by 42%. poultry increased by 44%. cattle increased by 34% 719 new borrowers (85% female) received credit from newly registered institutions. 43% of female involved in the planning process. 60% of ethnic involved in the planning process. 18 KESCs are found to be sustainability. 10 saving credit institutions were registered. 42 villages land use plans developed. A total of 92% (4673 households) have been obtained the lad use right certificates, out of which 619 (14.4%) households are female headed households. All registered VDRF have average operation self-sufficiency rate more than 110%
Output 4: All achieved. Annual workshops were timely conducted.
Project financial operation is steadily progressing with no cost overrun to date.
Audit report for FY 2013-2014 was timely submitted in June 2015.
Quarterly progress reports were submitted.
